title: Taught to his mother
hook: the Theravada story: the Buddha taught the Abhidhamma to his mother in heaven over one rainy season

segments.voice: Yesterday, a walk along the shelf of the third basket. Your line: seven books. What helped the thing on your shelf arise? Today the week closes, with the story of where those books came from. Day one thousand sixty-four.

The rains have come, and the Buddha is not on earth. That's how the Theravada story goes. A few days ago, on this path, he answered his rivals with the twin miracle at Savatthi, fire and water at once. Then, tradition says, he rose to a heaven above the world, a heaven of gods, and sat down to teach. In the crowd of gods who gathered to hear him was one he had come for. His mother, Maya, who died, tradition says, only days after he was born, and was reborn among the gods. He never knew her. Now he has a whole rainy season with her.
screen: `THE RAINS COME.` → `HE RISES TO A HEAVEN.` → `HIS MOTHER IS LISTENING.`

segments.voice: The story is told in the commentaries, and it's the Theravada answer to a question: where did the Abhidhamma come from? First, what he taught her. Not a short talk. The whole higher teaching, tradition says, the seven books we walked past yesterday, given over one rainy season. Second, how it reached the earth. Each day, the story goes, the Buddha came down to collect alms food, and met his disciple Sariputta. He gave Sariputta the outline of what he'd taught that day, the method, not every detail. And Sariputta, known for his wisdom, went back to the monks and taught it to them in full. So the tradition says the Abhidhamma comes from the Buddha, through Sariputta, to the monks. Third, why his mother. The commentaries don't make a speech about it. But the shape of the story is plain. The teaching that takes the mind apart into its smallest pieces was given first as a gift to the woman who gave him a body and then was gone. Some readers hear in it a son who never got to thank her, thanking her with what he had. Fourth, the descent. At the end of the rains, tradition says, he came back down to the world by a stairway of jewels at a place called Sankassa, with crowds waiting to welcome him. So this week closes on a gift. It started with Rohatsu and a week of sitting, ran through a day of miracles and the end of a year, opened the third basket, and lands here: a demanding teaching, given as a gift.
screen: `THE WHOLE TEACHING, ONE RAINY SEASON.` · `EACH DAY, AN OUTLINE TO SARIPUTTA.` · `A SON WHO NEVER GOT TO THANK HER.` · then, large: `DOWN A STAIRWAY OF JEWELS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like: honor your mother. Sit, and let the breath settle. Bring to mind your mother, or whoever mothered you: a grandmother, an aunt, a father who did it all, a teacher, a friend. Living, or gone. If that relationship is hard, choose whoever cared for you, even once, even a little. Hold them in mind without fixing anything. Then, on each out-breath, give them one thing you've learned, the way the Buddha gave his mother what he knew. A small thing is enough. The bell holds the time.
Taught to his mother. The Theravada story that the Buddha gave the whole Abhidhamma to his mother among the gods, over one rainy season. Today's word.

Your line: a gift to his mother. Today, pass one thing you know to someone who cared for you, a recipe, a trick, a story from this path, or say a thank you you never said. Day one thousand sixty-four.

howItsDone: Theravada Buddhists tell this story of the Abhidhamma's origin, and in some Theravada countries the end of the rains retreat is remembered as the time the Buddha came back down from teaching his mother.

what it means: the Theravada account of where the Abhidhamma came from: taught to his mother among the gods, passed through Sariputta to the monks.
what a scholar hears: the account comes from the commentaries, notably the Atthasalini and the Dhammapada commentary, and ties the third basket to the Buddha himself.
recall: the full moon of the birth

sources.ref: Atthasalini, introductory discourse (the Abhidhamma taught in the Tavatimsa heaven; the outline given to Sariputta)
Dhammapada commentary on verse 181 (the twin miracle, the rains in heaven, the descent at Sankassa)

notes: Maya's death 'only days after he was born' attributed to tradition (the usual account is seven days). Confirm.

Commentarial detail: Maya was reborn in the Tusita heaven and came to the Tavatimsa heaven to hear the teaching. The script says only 'reborn among the gods' and 'a heaven above the world'. Confirm this simplification is acceptable.
Daily alms and outline to Sariputta: per the Atthasalini (the Buddha went for alms to Uttarakuru and met Sariputta at Lake Anotatta). Simplified to 'came down to collect alms food'. Confirm.
Stairway 'of jewels' at Sankassa: the usual account has three stairways (gold, jewels, silver) made by Sakka; simplified. Confirm.
'A few days ago, on this path' refers to day 1059 (the twin miracle). The sequence twin miracle → rains in heaven follows the Dhammapada commentary.
howItsDone: the end of the rains remembered as the descent (e.g. Thadingyut in Myanmar, Tak Bat Devo in Thailand). Confirm wording.
Practice invites 'whoever mothered you' to stay welcoming to those whose mother is absent or whose relationship is hard.
